```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has a sourced, identifiable payer and price anchor: private practice physicians, with ClaireMed publishing $99/provider/month and S10.AI listing $99–$500/provider/month. A states outright that 'no clean single payer' was found.",
    "Every competitor named in A is free to the end user, funded by grants, VC or nonprofit dues. The only consumer-paid analog (Pointz) hides its price and needed $520k in outside funding. That makes a first paying customer within 90 days very unlikely for A.",
    "B's strongest negative evidence also cuts the other way. Cydoc, its documented failure case, still got four paying customers and $27,900 in revenue in 2024. A first paying customer is achievable even though scaling is hard. A offers no comparable proof that anyone pays for its product.",
    "B's Case For proposes a concrete narrowing: a note-draft layer that pastes into the existing EHR, possibly focused on psych reports, where Cydoc earned most of its revenue. This directly targets the $4–6k per-practice integration cost that sank Cydoc.",
    "A's suggested non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, insurers, data sales) appears only as speculation in the Case For and Open Questions, with no source showing any such buyer has paid a third party.",
    "B carries real risks that A does not: per-customer HIPAA BAAs, physician liability for AI-drafted notes, slow per-practice sales cycles, and better-funded direct competitors. B wins because it has a sourced payer, not because it is low-risk."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's claim of a 'credible non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants)' is unsourced. The only sourced funding example is BikeMaps.org's $930,000 grant to a research project, which is not evidence that a solo company could get one. A's demand evidence also rests on a single Hacker News seed quote plus competitor marketing copy. Neither shows willingness to pay.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs are thin on direct buyer evidence. B's demand evidence is one Reddit quote and an AMA statistic quoted second-hand from a competitor's marketing. Its 'apparent traction' for competitors is asserted without a source, and the Cydoc postmortem is a serious warning about sales-cycle length and integration cost. B wins mainly because A has no sourced payer, while B has published price points and a precedent that did convert paying customers."
}
```
